To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The criteria of effectiveness of organizations change in predictable ways over time as organizations develop through different stages of the organizational life cycle.

(1) the life cycle stage of the organization determines which of the four models of effectiveness will be the most important; (2) some shifts in life cycle stages are resisted more than others; and (3) contingency theory is not always applicable because the organization's response to its environment depends on its stage of development.
organizations in different stages in their life cycles are evaluated by different criteria of effectiveness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationships between stage in organizational life cycle and organizational effectiveness.
how the criteria of effectiveness change over time in the life of the organization and how the organization adapts itself to the environment in which it is embedded.
the relationships between life cycle stage and criteria of effectiveness and the implications of these relationships for organizational development interventions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
organizational effectiveness is a function of both the stage of development and the external environment of the organization.
organizational effectiveness is not a constant but a dynamic concept, and it varies in predictable ways as the organization moves through its life cycle.
the life cycle concept is useful in helping understand the relationships between organizations and their environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the organizational life cycle is an important contingency that must be considered in evaluating organizational effectiveness.
the effectiveness of organizations depends on their life cycles and the criteria of effectiveness that are appropriate in the particular life cycle stage.

the life cycle stage of an organization has a strong influence on the criteria of effectiveness that are appropriate for that organization and that the organization is likely to be more effective when the criteria used to evaluate it match those that are appropriate for its life cycle stage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organizational effectiveness is a dynamic concept that is related to the life cycle stage of the organization and the criteria of effectiveness that are most relevant to it.
organizations are not static entities but rather are in a constant process of growth and change.
organizations are not static entities, and that they change over time in predictable ways.
